factual_claims.source_evidence: Income Statement (page 44) reports other operating income of DKK 2,026k; Financial Review (page 29) mentions a strategic agreement with a sales partner contributed to operating income.

factual_claims.claim: In the second half, EBITDA was positive at DKK 0.5 million, compared with a loss of DKK 3.6 million in the same period of 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Periodic Reporting (page 24) explicitly states H2 2025 EBITDA was DKK 0.5m vs H2 2024 loss of DKK 3.6m.

factual_claims.claim: Recurring revenue indicators also improved.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics section (page 25) highlights growth in CARR, new sales, and customer metrics, indicating improved recurring revenue performance.

factual_claims.claim: Contracted annual recurring revenue increased 15% to DKK 24.4 million, above the company’s guidance of DKK 23–24 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics (page 25) reports CARR grew 15% to DKK 24.4m; Outlook 2026 (page 32) states guidance was DKK 23–24m.

factual_claims.claim: New sales rose 45% to DKK 4.5 million, 52 new customers were added compared with 45 in 2024, and average contracted revenue per customer increased to DKK 87,000 from DKK 70,000.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics (page 25) confirms new sales of DKK 4.5m (45% YoY increase), 52 new customers (vs 45 in 2024), and average CARR per customer rising from TDKK 70 to TDKK 87.

factual_claims.claim: Lower marketing costs reduced customer acquisition costs by 32%, cutting the CAC payback period from 43 to 23 months and improving the CLV/CAC ratio from 2.7 to 4.1.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics (page 25) states CAC payback period fell to 23 months from 43 months and CLV/CAC rose to 4.1 from 2.7, attributing this to reduced marketing costs.

factual_claims.claim: The Rule of 40 score improved from minus 40% to 17%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics (page 25) explicitly states the Rule of 40 score improved to 17% at year-end 2025 from -40% in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: However, ARR churn increased to 12.6% from 10.5%, while net retention remained unchanged at 94%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics (page 26) reports ARR churn rate rose to 12.6% from 10.5% and net retention stayed at 94%.

factual_claims.claim: Management attributed higher churn among established customers partly to increased demand for FP&A functionality and ERP systems meeting the needs of smaller groups.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics (page 26) notes churn increased due to customer demand for FP&A tools; Letter from CEO (page 8) and Product section (page 18) discuss FP&A expansion addressing this need.

factual_claims.claim: The company’s transition from a consolidation product to the broader Konsolidator Suite was a central development.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Strategy section (page 12) and Product section (page 18) detail the shift to a full financial reporting suite including FP&A, data management, and analytics.

factual_claims.claim: It introduced financial data management and analytics capabilities, began developing FP&A, and signed its first FP&A customers ahead of the January 2026 launch.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Product section (page 18) states financial data management launched in April 2025, FP&A development began in May 2025, and first FP&A customers were signed in December 2025 ahead of the January 2026 launch.

factual_claims.claim: Partner-led growth expanded, with 38% of new customers acquired through partners versus 22% in 2024, including the Exsitec partnership covering sales and customer success in Sweden and Norway.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Letter from CEO (page 8) states 38% of new customers came through partners in 2025 vs 22% in 2024; Key Events (page 9) highlights the Exsitec partnership.

factual_claims.claim: Operating cash flow improved to negative DKK 1.0 million from negative DKK 9.2 million, supported by lower losses, earlier invoicing, annual customer payments, and longer vendor payment terms.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash Flow Statement (page 45) shows operating cash flow of DKK (1,047k) in 2025 vs DKK (9,171k) in 2024; Financial Review (page 30) cites lower losses, earlier invoicing, annual payments, and extended vendor terms as drivers.

factual_claims.claim: Net cash flow was positive by DKK 11,000 after DKK 4.8 million raised through private placements, but year-end cash was only DKK 0.4 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash Flow Statement (page 45) reports net cash flow of DKK 11k; page 24 notes DKK 4.8m raised via private placements; Balance Sheet (page 46) shows cash and cash equivalents of DKK 370k at year-end.

factual_claims.claim: Consolidated equity remained negative at DKK 3.6 million, although parent-company equity was positive at DKK 0.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Balance Sheet (page 46) shows consolidated equity of DKK (3,583k) (~DKK 3.6m); Parent Company Balance Sheet (page 65) shows equity of DKK 701k (~DKK 0.7m).

factual_claims.claim: For 2026, Konsolidator guides for CARR and revenue of DKK 27–29 million and positive EBITDA of DKK 1–2 million, while prioritizing churn reduction, operational cash generation, and refinancing of its loans.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Outlook 2026 (page 32) provides guidance for CARR and revenue of DKK 27–29m and EBITDA of DKK 1–2m; Strategic Outlook (page 32) emphasizes churn reduction, operational cash flow, and loan refinancing as priorities.
